summary: Evening spike of 5xx on streaming route during autoscaler scale-down (GPU preempt + TLS affinity break)
description:
Issue summary: Between ~19:22 and 19:45 UTC on 2026-03-10 we observed a sharp elevation in 5xx errors for the customer-facing streaming chat route for Nimbus Health (enterprise). The failures were primarily 502/503 on the API gateway and upstream runtime returning abrupt stream termination. Impact: multiple customers experienced dropped streaming responses and retries resulting in degraded UX for embedded chat in production. Intermittent but repeatable during autoscaler scale-down events.

Observed behavior:
- API gateway logs show many upstream 502/503s and TLS handshake reset entries coincident with autoscaler drain events.
- Serving runtime logs show SIGTERM followed by NVML driver resets and abrupt process reaper activity for some worker threads.
- Customers reported partial transcripts and immediate connection resets rather than graceful stream closure.

Why this is likely critical: streaming requests are long-lived; a poor drain during scale-down can cause in-flight sessions to be killed and reconnect attempts to hit different backends causing TLS/ALPN affinity mismatches and hedged retries amplify the problem.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create sustained long-lived streaming sessions to prod streaming endpoint (chat) using customer tenancy for Nimbus Health
2) Trigger autoscaler scale-down (simulate low traffic or schedule a downscale window),
3) Observe API gateway 502/503 spike and serving-runtime SIGTERM + NVML logs,
4) Reproduce with smaller scale to validate timing window for connection drain failures.
logs_snippets: [apigw] 2026-03-10T19:23:12Z upstream 502 tcp: TLS handshake reset: EOF while reading response headers
[runtime] 2026-03-10T19:23:13Z SIGTERM received: initiating shutdown, inflight streams: 128
[nvml] 2026-03-10T19:23:14Z NVML: GPU reset detected on device 0 (driver=520.61)
[kube] 2026-03-10T19:23:15Z PreStop hook timeout reached; container terminated
investigation_notes: Checked autoscaler events: scale-down triggered at 19:22:54 UTC; target pool size reduced by 2 nodes.
Correlated occurrence window with elevated 5xx: 19:22:50--19:25:00 UTC (spike aligns almost exactly).
Kernel & NVML logs show GPU reset events immediately after SIGTERM; hypothesis: driver-level reset when process is terminated before KV cache flush completes.
API gateway logs include repeated TLS session errors (ALPN mismatch) when clients reconnected to new backends after termination.
Rate of hedged retries at apigw increased 3x during the window causing retry amplification.
mitigation_actions: 1) Short-term: applied a canary configuration to api-gateway to reduce hedged retry concurrency for streaming routes (limit 2 concurrent hedged attempts).
2) Increased serving-runtime pod terminationGracePeriodSeconds from 30s -> 90s in us-east canary to allow drains for long-lived streams.
3) Temporarily pinned autoscaler to floor of 6 nodes in the affected pool until drains validated.
4) Notified Nimbus Health CS contact and recommended client-side backoff adjustments; opened coordination channel #support-nimbus to inform on progress.
resolution: Deployed a staged fix: increased terminationGracePeriodSeconds to 90s and added a preStop sleep+drain hook for the serving-runtime in us-east. Autoscaler floor enforced for the short term (6 nodes) to avoid repeated preemptions during peak evening hours for enterprise customers. Also reduced hedged retry aggressiveness on streaming routes in api-gateway to avoid amplification. Post-deploy monitoring for 48 hours showed 5xx rate returned to baseline and no further NVML resets correlated with scale-down events. Incident closed after customer confirmation that errors stopped impacting their users.
follow_up_actions: 1) Runbook update: add explicit streaming drain checklist and autoscaler constraints for tenant-critical times (owner: SRE team).
2) Long-term: implement connection handoff mechanism to transfer active KV cache/state between runtimes during drain (owner: serving-runtime eng).
3) Alerting: create a composite alert for simultaneous (autoscaler-scale event + NVML reset + apigw-502-rate) to catch this mode earlier.
4) Coordinate with customer to test a controlled scale-down window and validate client reconnection behavior.
comments: 2026-03-10 19:28 - Support (Ava Chen): Customer reported sudden wave of streaming disconnects across multiple users. Collected initial logs and escalated to SRE.

2026-03-10 19:40 - SRE (Diego Martinez): Observed GPU resets in kernel logs immediately after SIGTERM on several runtime pods. Correlating with kuedev autoscaler events. Hypothesis: pods are being terminated while heavy KV flush is happening; preStop hook timing is insufficient.
2026-03-10 20:02 - Eng (Priya Kaur): Pushed a canary bump for terminationGracePeriodSeconds and added a preStop sleep+drain. Monitoring now. Reduced hedged retry concurrency at apigw.

2026-03-11 08:10 - Customer (Nimbus Health - Ops): Confirmed reduced errors overnight after the fix. They saw a single reconnect but no transcript loss. Requested a postmortem and permanent config change.
2026-03-12 11:05 - Support (Ava Chen): Marked resolved after 48h of stable telemetry and customer confirmation. Added follow-ups into SRE backlog.
